title: The Equal Sign and Missing Numbers
seo_title: Grade 1 Equal Sign and Missing Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 1.5E)
standard_text: 1.5E understand that the equal sign represents a relationship where expressions on each side of the equal sign represent the same value(s); 1.5F determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation when the unknown may be any one of the three or four terms in the equation
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 worksheets for Texas TEKS 1.5E and 1.5F: the meaning of the equal sign, true or false number sentences and missing numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: = means both sides have the same value.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The equal sign means both sides have the same value.
  • 8 = 3 + 5 is true. 4 + 4 = 3 + 5 is true too.
  • To find a missing number, make both sides the same: 6 + ☐ = 10, so ☐ = 4.

Examples

Example

4 + ☐ = 3 + 6

3 + 6 = 9

4 + 5 = 9

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking = means “the answer is next”= means the same as.
Adding all the numbers4 + ☐ = 3 + 6 is not 13.
Calling 8 = 3 + 5 falseThe total can be on the left.

sets.title: Word problems with a missing number

items.q: Nevaeh has 7 shells. She needs 12 shells. How many more shells does she need?
items.e: Think: 7 + ? = 12. Count up from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5. 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Marcus has 9 stickers. He gets some more. Now he has 13 stickers. How many stickers did he get?
items.e: Think: 9 + ? = 13. Count up from 9 to 13: 10, 11, 12, 13. That is 4. 9 + 4 = 13.

items.q: Some birds are in a tree. 6 more birds come. Now there are 15 birds. How many birds were in the tree at first?
items.e: Think: ? + 6 = 15. Take away the 6 that came: 15 − 6 = 9. Check: 9 + 6 = 15.

items.q: Sofia had 16 grapes. She ate some. Now she has 10 grapes. How many grapes did she eat?
items.e: Think: 16 − ? = 10. Count up from 10 to 16: 10 + 6 = 16. So the answer is 6. Check: 16 − 6 = 10.

items.q: Some kids are at the park. 4 kids go home. Now 8 kids are at the park. How many kids were at the park at first?
items.e: Think: ? − 4 = 8. Put back the 4 kids who left: 8 + 4 = 12. Check: 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: A box holds 10 crayons. There are 7 crayons in it now. How many more crayons fit in the box?
items.e: The box holds 10. 7 are in it. Count up from 7 to 10: 8, 9, 10. That is 3. 7 + 3 = 10.

items.q: Isabella wants to read 17 pages. She has read 8 pages. How many more pages does she need to read?
items.e: Think: 8 + ? = 17. From 8 to 10 is 2. From 10 to 17 is 7. 2 + 7 = 9. So 8 + 9 = 17.

items.q: Ethan has 13 toy cars. He gives some to Emma. Now Ethan has 5 toy cars. How many toy cars did he give?
items.e: Think: 13 − ? = 5. Count up from 5 to 13: 5 + 8 = 13. So the answer is 8. Check: 13 − 8 = 5.

items.q: There are 10 ducks. Some ducks are in the water. 6 ducks are on the grass. How many ducks are in the water?
Gabriel has 8 marbles. Liam has 3 marbles. How many more marbles does Gabriel have than Liam?
items.e: Think: 3 + ? = 8. Count up from 3: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 5 more.

items.q: A plate has 6 cookies. Dad puts some more on it. Now there are 14 cookies. How many cookies did Dad put on?
items.e: Think: 6 + ? = 14. From 6 to 10 is 4. From 10 to 14 is 4. 4 + 4 = 8. So 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: There are 18 children in a class. 9 are boys. The rest are girls. How many girls are there?
Elijah has some stamps. Ava gives him 7 more. Now Elijah has 17 stamps. How many stamps did Elijah have at first?
items.e: Think: ? + 7 = 17. Take away the 7 that came: 17 − 7 = 10. Check: 10 + 7 = 17.

items.q: Mateo needs 20 points to win a game. He has 12 points. How many more points does he need?
Ximena has 5 red blocks and 3 blue blocks. Luis has 6 blocks. How many more blocks does Luis need to have as many as Ximena?
items.e: Ximena has 5 + 3 = 8 blocks. Think: 6 + ? = 8. Count up from 6: 7, 8. That is 2. 5 + 3 = 6 + 2.

items.q: Carlos has 4 red apples and 4 green apples. Harper has 2 red apples and some green apples. They have the same number of apples. How many green apples does Harper have?
items.e: Carlos has 4 + 4 = 8 apples. Harper must have 8 too. Think: 2 + ? = 8. 2 + 6 = 8, so 6. 4 + 4 = 2 + 6.

items.q: Aaliyah has 7 shells. She needs 12. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: She has 7 and needs 12 in all. 7 and some more make 12: 7 + ? = 12.

items.q: There are 15 frogs. Some hop away. 9 frogs are left. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: Start with 15. Some hop away, so take away. 9 are left: 15 − ? = 9.

items.q: Zoe has some pens. She gets 4 more. Now she has 11. Which number sentence fits?
items.e: She starts with some pens. That is ?. Then 4 more come, and the total is 11: ? + 4 = 11.

items.q: Diego has 6 big bears and 2 small bears. Jayden has 8 bears. Which number sentence shows they have the same?
items.e: Diego has 6 + 2 bears. Jayden has 8. The same number goes on each side: 6 + 2 = 8.
